purpose: Define the governed football-only rules that may convert an existing Walters personnel loss into a game-specific matchup value without changing the underlying player-value registry, carried team rating, or current Graham board during Stage M1.

sourceAuthority.primary: Billy Walters with Armen Keteyian, Gambler, Chapters 21-22
governingPrinciples: All relevant football variables must ultimately be expressed in point-spread-equivalent units.
Published player rankings are starting inputs only; game-specific football mechanics may make the same player materially more or less valuable in a particular matchup.
A matchup adjustment must begin from the governed healthy-player value, governed replacement value, current availability, and verified role already established by the personnel system.
A matchup adjustment is a game-specific overlay and may not silently alter the frozen player-value registry or carried team power rating.
Market reaction may never be used to infer or calibrate matchup value.

sourceLockedExample.description: The existing personnel calibration preserves Walters' example that Tristan Wirfs could be worth substantially more in a particular Rams matchup than his ordinary player value because the opponent pass rush, backup situation, and cascading protection effects change the football consequences of the absence.
sourceLockedExample.rule: Do not generalize the example into a universal multiplier or cap.

marketIsolation.rule: Matchup screening, evidence collection, scoring and shadow calculation must be completed before any contemporaneous market comparison is viewed.

baseValueRule.normalPersonnelLossFormula: normalTeamLoss = healthyValue - replacementValue for an unavailable healthy starter, after any already-governed effectiveness and cluster treatment
baseValueRule.startingAuthority: Use only values produced by the active Walters personnel calibration and production ledger.
baseValueRule.noRevaluation: Stage M1 may not change healthyValue, replacementValue, Madden OVR bands, QB bands, or carried team ratings.

candidateWhen: a positive-value blocker is unavailable, limited, or replaced by a materially weaker verified player
the opponent has a verified high-impact pass-rush player or front expected to attack the affected protection area
the missing player's role and replacement assignment are sufficiently resolved
requiredFootballEvidence: opponent pressure source or front structure

candidateWhen: a positive-value coverage or receiving player is unavailable, limited, or materially replaced
the opposing offense/defense has a verified primary target, alignment, or coverage responsibility that interacts directly with the loss
the expected replacement and assignment are sufficiently resolved
requiredFootballEvidence: expected opposing primary matchup or usage

candidateWhen: the unavailable or limited defender/offensive player has a material middle-field, receiving, coverage, or tackling role
the opponent is expected to stress that role through tight ends, backs, slot usage, or intermediate middle-field concepts
the replacement role is sufficiently resolved
a material run-blocking, run-defense, tackling, or ball-carrier role is degraded
the opponent's expected rushing structure directly stresses that role
the replacement and assignment are sufficiently resolved
multiple protection roles are degraded or one loss forces a verified secondary protection change
the opponent has a front or rusher capable of exploiting the resulting protection change
the cascade is described with explicit football mechanics rather than generic injury accumulation
requiredFootballEvidence: which additional player or unit role is affected
why the opponent can exploit the cascade

screeningRules.materialityGate: Do not open a matchup case merely because two opposing players are highly rated. There must be a current personnel, role, or availability change whose normal personnel value could plausibly be materially altered by the opponent-specific football mechanics.

numericGovernance.shadowFormulaForLaterStages: matchupAdjustedTeamLoss = normalTeamLoss + approvedMatchupIncrement; pointsToHomeSpread follows the existing home/away sign convention
numericGovernance.approvedMatchupIncrement: Must remain null in Stage M1. Stage M2 may populate a shadow-only increment only after the matchup family, evidence, normal loss, replacement and football mechanism all pass review.
numericGovernance.negativeAdjustmentMeaning: A specific opponent can make the normal personnel loss less damaging than baseline; any reduction must be supported to the same standard as amplification.
numericGovernance.rounding: Preserve exact internal arithmetic; live half-point board rounding remains outside Stage M1 and is not invoked.

doubleCountGuard.personnel: The normal healthy-minus-replacement loss is the starting point and may be counted once only.
doubleCountGuard.clusters: If a governed receiver or defensive-line cluster multiplier has already changed the normal personnel loss, Stage M2 must begin from that post-cluster loss and may not reapply the cluster effect.
doubleCountGuard.teamRating: Never carry a temporary matchup overlay into currentRating.
doubleCountGuard.gameFactors: Home field, venue, rest, travel and weather remain separate game adjustments and may not be restated as matchup value.
doubleCountGuard.postgame: TGPL/injury-environment learning may not carry a completed pregame matchup overlay forward a second time.

required: no live board mutation from M1
Week 1 candidate screen completed across all active games
candidate cases contain resolved football roles and sourceRefs
shadow arithmetic can be reproduced from the existing personnel ledger
